events.stem:
Consider the following reactions. In each, look at the product that contains the named element (balanced equations are not needed).
(i) CuO, >1100°C  →  product containing Cu
(ii) Au, NaCN, O₂, cyanide process, air  →  product containing Au
(iii) Cr₂O₇²⁻, H⁺, reducing agent, acid medium  →  product containing Cr
(iv) FeS₂, O₂, roasting in excess air  →  product containing Fe
(v) ZnS, O₂, roasting at >850°C with controlled air  →  product containing Zn
(vi) Cu(OH)₂, heating  →  product containing Cu
(vii) Na₂CrO₄, H₂SO₄, acidification, crystallisation of Na₂SO₄ at >32°C  →  product containing Cr
(viii) CuSO₄, KI, excess KI  →  product containing Cu
The number of reactions in which that product is diamagnetic is
Give the answer as an integer.

members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction and determine its magnetic nature (diamagnetic vs paramagnetic). Diamagnetic species have all electrons paired. Evaluate typical products:
(i) CuO heated >1100°C reduces to Cu metal (Cu⁰). Elemental Cu is diamagnetic (Cu has 3d10 4s1? Actually Cu ground state is 3d10 4s1, but in bulk metal all electrons paired? Cu metal is paramagnetic due to conduction electrons? However typical exam context: elemental Cu is paramagnetic? Need check: Cu metal is paramagnetic with small susceptibility. But many simple problems treat elemental metals as diamagnetic? However Cu2+ is paramagnetic. Likely product is Cu2O or CuO? Reaction CuO >1100°C may decompose to Cu and O2? Usually CuO stable. Might produce Cu2O? Not sure. Assume product is CuO (Cu2+) paramagnetic. But phrase 'product containing Cu' could be CuO itself. However heating CuO alone likely remains CuO. So product CuO (Cu2+) paramagnetic.
(ii) Au in cyanide process yields AuCN or Na3AuCN4? Final product Au metal precipitate (Au0) diamagnetic.
(iii) Cr2O7^2- reduced in acid yields Cr3+ (d3) paramagnetic.
(iv) FeS2 roasting yields Fe2O3 (Fe3+) paramagnetic.
(v) ZnS roasting yields ZnO (Zn2+ d10) diamagnetic.
(vi) Cu(OH)2 heating yields CuO (Cu2+) paramagnetic.
(vii) Na2CrO4 acidified yields CrO3 or Cr2O3? Likely Cr2O3 (Cr3+) paramagnetic.
(viii) CuSO4 + excess KI gives CuI (Cu+) d10 diamagnetic.
Thus diamagnetic products: (ii) Au metal, (v) ZnO, (viii) CuI. Possibly (i) if Cu metal formed. But typical roasting CuO stays CuO. So count 3.
Thus answer 3.
